title: Methanol Precipitation of Proteins
author: Tobias von der Haar
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.icecate

steps.title: Select and Prepare Container
steps.instruction: Choose a centrifugation-compatible container large enough to accommodate the sample and additional reagents based on the following maximal sample size ratios (tube volume: maximal sample volume): 1.5 ml: 0.16 ml; 2 ml: 0.22 ml; 10 ml: 1.1 ml; 15 ml: 1.6 ml; 50 ml: 5.5 ml.

substeps.instruction: Place the sample in the selected container.
Note the sample volume to calculate reagent amounts for subsequent steps.

steps.title: Initial Methanol Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate proteins using methanol and centrifugation.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 volumes of methanol to the tube.
Centrifuge at 9000 g, 4°C for ten minutes.

steps.title: Remove Aqueous Phase
steps.instruction: Separate the phases by removing the upper layer.

substeps.instruction: Identify the two phases: an upper aqueous phase and a lower solvent phase (protein is at the interface).
Pipet away and discard the upper aqueous phase, ensuring the interface is not disturbed.

steps.title: Further Solvent Extraction and Washing
steps.instruction: Perform a secondary precipitation and wash sequence.

substeps.instruction: Mix the sample with 4 volumes of methanol and vortex.
Add 1 volume of chloroform and vortex again.
Add 3 volumes of water and vortex.
Centrifuge at 9000 g, 4°C for five minutes.

steps.title: Dry and Dissolve Pellet
steps.instruction: Recover the protein pellet and resuspend it.

substeps.instruction: Dry the pellet by standing the tube open and upside down on a clean, dry tissue.
Dissolve the pellet in an appropriate volume of buffer (e.g., SDS sample buffer for SDS PAGE analysis).
